method: Single-author visual review of pinned-font stills at 1280x720, 1440x900 and 1920x1080 plus rendered motion. Subjective, not independent user research. Scores describe each view, not the worst individual axis.

screens.label: Home / living room
screens.note: A motivated window and lamp, a layered room and expressive portrait make the first view inviting. The existing gameplay actor still has a different silhouette from the new portrait.

screens.label: Inventory
screens.note: Larger art, quiet empty slots, inset plinths and labeled rarity tiers improve scanning. Equipment illustration itself is unchanged.

screens.label: Boss fight
screens.note: An integer-scaled arena, chapter lighting, named boss, HP trail and bounded impact improve the encounter. A full household-boss redraw remains open.

screens.label: Forge
screens.note: The hearth gives the selected item a physical place and the three columns a clear center. Dense recipe controls remain the existing workflow.

screens.label: Market
screens.note: A larger collectible and warm selected row improve focus. The sparse listing table still feels administrative; no fictional listings were added.

screens.label: Gear detail / v2 upgrade path
screens.note: A larger selected item, readable comparison and clear primary action. V2 upgrades through craft/equip; the separate classic Upgrade screen is unchanged and documented separately.

screens.label: Relic detail
screens.note: Collectible art is more prominent, with all contract facts retained. Existing metadata art remains unchanged and could gain more character later.

screens.label: Forge reveal
screens.note: Crafted art, a warm reveal sweep and tiered fanfare connect the action to the result. The common result is deliberately restrained; bespoke great-success presentation remains open.
